findings.where: Screen 2 (The turning field), also the screen 4 chart
findings.what: The example motor is never stated on screen, so 1125 rpm, 1440 rpm and the 1500 rpm axis appear with no rule behind them; say once on screen 2: 'Assume a 230 V, 50 Hz, four-pole motor. Its field turns at 120 × 50 ÷ 4 = 1500 rpm. The switch opens at 75% of that, 1125 rpm. On its fan it runs at 1440 rpm.' (checked by hand: 1500 and 1125 are right).

findings.where: Screen 2 phasor panel and the screen 3 Why
findings.what: The 9.82 A, 6.00 A, 50.2°, 20.1° and 30.1° come from example windings (main 15 Ω with 18 Ω reactance, start 36 Ω with 13.2 Ω) that never appear on screen, so the impedance-triangle working the brief promised is hidden; show it in two short lines, such as 'Main: arctan(18 ÷ 15) = 50.2° behind. Start: arctan(13.2 ÷ 36) = 20.1° behind. Gap 30.1°.' (checked by hand: √549 = 23.43 Ω, 230 ÷ 23.43 = 9.82 A, √1470.24 = 38.34 Ω, 230 ÷ 38.34 = 6.00 A, 50.2 − 20.1 = 30.1°, all correct).

findings.where: Screen 4 Running row, and the screen 2 status line 'the turning rotor still gets torque from it'
findings.what: Why a pulsing field keeps a turning rotor going is stated but never explained, because explain.text (a pulsing field acts like two equal fields turning opposite ways, and once the rotor turns the one going with it pulls harder) never shows in a steps lesson; put those two short sentences on screen 4's Running row.

The torque bar and readout still step down from 190% to 110% at 1125 rpm while the status says the start winding is still in, which contradicts the lesson's 'the switch opens and the torque drops a step'; keep the torque on the both-windings line while the start winding is fed, or say on screen that it is drawn as for a working switch.

The screen runs to 98 words across five cards, over the 90-word limit; trim, for example 'Safety: Isolate, lock off and prove dead.' and a shorter Resistance row ('The two windings read in parallel, so lower than either. Reading the main winding alone? The start circuit is open.').
The read runs to 101 words, over 90; drop the closing stuck-open and stuck-closed sentences, which screen 6 already gives, or merge the wound-like-the-main sentences.

findings.where: Screen 1 text and drawing, and the Keep this rule line 'Main and start windings 90° apart'
findings.what: Say '90 electrical degrees' once, because on a four-pole motor he will see the two windings 45° apart when he opens it; a short label like 'one pole pair drawn' on the ring would make the right angle honest.

'Starting torque: Low: typically…', 'Starting current: High: …' and 'Safety first: Isolate, … prove dead first.' read clumsily with two colons and a doubled 'first'; write 'Starting torque: low, typically 100 to 175% of rated.' and similar.
'It goes with the sine of the angle between the currents' leaves out the currents themselves; say 'It goes with both currents and the sine of the angle between them', as the Keep this card does.

findings.where: Keep this card, rule line 'Im × Is × sin(angle between them)'
findings.what: Im and Is are not defined anywhere on screen; write 'main current × start current × sine of the angle between them'.

findings.where: Keep this card, 'Example: 4.5 Ω and 15 Ω windings read 3.46 Ω together'
findings.what: The figure first appears on the card with no working, because the worked example sits in practice.text, which never shows; add '4.5 × 15 ÷ 19.5 = 3.46 Ω' (checked by hand: 67.5 ÷ 19.5 = 3.46) or move the example onto screen 6.
'It overheats and burns, then the overload trips' is surer than the source, which says only that the winding can be damaged; say 'It overheats and can burn out. The overload may trip first.'

The right answer is the second button on both checks, and on screen 7 it is also by far the longest option; move one right answer to first or third place and shorten it to 'The start circuit is open'.

findings.where: Screen 3, hint for 'To give it more inductance, so its current lags more'
findings.what: 'Lagging less than the main is what puts the two out of step' is too absolute, since a current lagging more would also be out of step; say 'Thin wire and fewer turns can only make it lag less, and that is what puts the two out of step.'

The phasor panel, readouts, status line and torque bar sit about 700 px below the ring, behind the controls, so on a phone he cannot watch the field turn and see the angle or the torque step at the same time; put the readouts and status line straight under the ring on narrow screens.

findings.where: Screen 2, 'Angle between currents' readout with the switch stuck open
findings.what: It reads 'start winding out', which sounds like the switch dropped it out normally; 'not fed' would match the panel's 'start: not fed' and the status line.
The slanted blade reads as an open contact to an electrician's eye, though the lesson says it is drawn closed (as it is at rest); draw the blade on its contact or add the label 'closed at rest'.
